findings.title: Condition tests only compare SQL text, and the caching tests were deleted
findings.body: Most tests now assert `toEqual(Prisma.sql`...`)`, which only checks that the SQL string and values match. Any reformatting or parenthesisation change breaks them, and they do not check what the SQL returns. Only the `getBaseConditions` test runs a query, and it covers just the user scope with both filters. The org and team scopes and the eventTypeId and memberUserId filters are never run against the DB. The two "Caching" tests were removed, but `cachedAuthConditions` and `cachedFilterConditions` still exist in `insightsBooking.ts:49-50`. Consider adding queries for the org and team scopes. Consider restoring a caching test, for example by spying on the repository and checking it is called once.

contracts.action: Replace Prisma where-input conditions with raw Prisma.Sql fragments, and replace findMany with getBaseConditions
contracts.equivalent_path: The previous findMany at the same location AND-ed the auth and filter where-inputs. The new code returns a Sql fragment for callers to embed in $queryRaw.
contracts.before_after: Before: auth conditions and filter conditions were combined and passed to prisma.findMany. After: they are combined with `(auth) AND (filter)`. The OR inside the eventTypeId filter is parenthesised when it is combined, so precedence is preserved (lines 105-122). The `1=0` fallback replaces `id:-1`. An empty team-scope user list is now omitted, which matches the old `userId in []` clause matching nothing.
contracts.visible_effect: No UI path calls this service yet. A repo-wide search found only the integration test as a caller.
contracts.failure_mode: Values are bound as parameters, so there is no injection risk. Column names are hardcoded quoted identifiers, and `ANY(${array})` is already used elsewhere in the repo (PermissionRepository). A caller that forgets to apply the Sql gets no scoping, but no such caller exists today.

summary: The rewrite from Prisma where-inputs to raw `Prisma.sql` is logically equivalent to the old behaviour. Operator precedence is preserved through parenthesised reduces, values are parameterised, and no other callers exist. One minor test-coverage point: the SQL-text assertions are brittle and the caching tests were dropped.
